“The last thing that I would want is somebody to have the shock of finding out on social media or on television about their home being lost,” British Columbia Emergency Management Minister Kelly Greene said.
Eby said the province would review the response, including whether changes are needed to wildfire planning, building standards and vegetation management near communities.
Given the drought and summer heat, he warned, “this is very unlikely to be the last significant fire we see this summer.”
Summerland Mayor Doug Holmes warned that recovery would be long and difficult.
Canada has endured a series of severe wildfire seasons in recent years, with smoke repeatedly drifting into the United States. In record-setting 2023, fires burned more than 14.6 million hectares (36 million acres), an area roughly the size of Illinois.
Canada has warmed faster than the global average in recent decades, while the amount of land burned by wildfires has increased substantially. Much of the country’s forest is remote and dominated by spruce and pine, conditions that can make fires difficult to contain once they become established.

In August 2026, people shared a video allegedly showing U.S. President Donald Trump waking himself up with a fart while seated during an Oval Office announcement.
For example, on Aug. 8, an X user posted (archived) the clip overlaid with text reading, "Trump wakes himself up after audible fart during White House briefing."
Other users shared the same video on Facebook (archived), Instagram (archived), TikTok (archived), X (archived) and YouTube (archived). A number of Snopes readers also searched for information about the rumor.
In sum, Snopes' investigation found that someone edited a sound effect into the video. A YouTube video titled "Top 10 fart meme sound effects" features the exact same fart sound effect at the 0:16 mark. As such, we rated the claim as fake.
During the clip, Trump's eyes appear partially or fully closed for several seconds. He does not slowly drop his head or display other sleepy signs we previously examined in reported instances of him appearing to begin dozing off.
The clip originated from a longer video with Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, speaking and referring to Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., during a White House announcement about maternal healthcare on May 11, 2026. The same moment from the altered fart video users shared begins at the 20:24 mark:
We emailed the White House to ask if the administration wished to respond to the users editing and sharing videos with edited-in fart noises and will update this article if we receive a response.
Researching the rumor
The Trump video with the added fart sound effect featured Oz's voice, recognizable from his former daytime TV show, "The Dr. Oz Show." Oz did not visibly appear in the cropped clip users shared on social media. In the video, Oz mentions the name Katie — a reference to Britt — and the word "fertility."
To find the source of the clip, we performed a single Google search for the four terms "Katie," "Dr. Mehmet Oz," "Oval Office" and "fertility." The results led to the May 11 maternal healthcare announcement at the White House, including the aforementioned YouTube video of the full event.
To find the fart sound effect that was added, we initially surmised the person who edited in the noise likely sourced the audio from a popular video appearing high in Google search results. A Google search for "fart sound effect" (without quotation marks) first displayed results for three videos. We located the match at the No. 6 slot in the earlier-mentioned "top 10" video.
A reverse image search indicated TikTok user @brilliant.gomez possibly shared the first post (archived) of the edited video on Aug. 7. We messaged that user to ask whether they created the clip and will update this story if we receive further details.
James Kennedy, an Australian creator and podcaster, has regularly shared videos of Trump and members of his administration with added fart sound effects, including most recently on Aug. 10.
Searches of Kennedy's comedic content on his Facebook, Instagram, Threads and TikTok accounts did not yet locate the same clip from the May 11 Oval Office announcement, possibly suggesting another user edited the video. We contacted Kennedy to ask whether he created the clip and will update this article if we receive further details.
For further reading, we previously reported about one of Kennedy's videos supposedly showing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth farting at the beginning of a Pentagon news conference.

Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa after admitting he joined Manchester United because it is a bigger club than his former team.
Tielemans made a £35 million ($47 million) move to Old Trafford in July when United triggered a release clause in his Villa contract.
The Belgium midfielder helped Villa end its 30-year trophy drought by winning the Europa League last season.
But Tielemans had no qualms about joining United, which finished one spot above fourth-placed Villa in the Premier League last season.
“There are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them,” he said recently.
Few would deny United has a far greater global profile than Emery’s men, but Villa supporters were upset by Tielemans’ suggestion this week that their club are smaller than the 20-time English champion.
Tielemans, who joined Villa from Leicester in 2023, took to social media to make peace with his old club.
“Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or the institution of Aston Villa Football Club, which I massively respect and I’m grateful for the past 3 years,” the 29-year-old wrote on Instagram on Thursday.
“I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, will be more careful in the future.
“Wishing the club the best in the future.”
Tielemans, who scored in Villa’s Europa League final win against Freiburg, described his move to United as “the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football”.
He is expected to make his first Premier League appearance for United in its season opener at Hull on August 22.

Srinagar, Aug 13: After evading police for 35 years, a terrorist responsible for the 1991 Jammu railway station bomb blast was arrested in Anantnag district, police said on Thursday.
Police said accused Altaf Hussain Sheikh was brought before the TADA Court, and further legal proceedings will be initiated.
They said Sheikh had concealed his identity and been living as a businessman.
According to the police, aSheikh, along with three other accomplices, carried out the bombing at platform number 1, killing three people, including two paramilitary personnel, and injuring 18 civilians.
While one operative, Aman Ullah Khan, was arrested on the day of the blast, the other three went into hiding.
On Thursday, the Jammu Railway Police traced Sheikh to Anantnag and arrested him.
"Railway (GRP) Police Jammu arrests an absconding terrorist booked under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act. Altaf Hussain Sheikh, son of Nazir Ahmed Sheikh, resident of Marhama-Bijbehara, Anantnag, after a long chase of 35 years, initially went underground and was living with a concealed identity for several decades," police said in a statement.
"During the investigation, one accused, Aman Ullah Khan, was arrested, while three other accused persons escaped and could not be arrested at that time and were declared absconders by the concerned court," the police said.
Police said that the Railway police intensified their manhunt over the past two years, eventually finding him disguised as a successful businessman in the Bijbehara area.
“ In the last two years, the railway police, Jammu, launched an intensive manhunt and identified the accused Altaf Hussain Sheikh, verified his identity by minutely going into details of his identity and residential particulars and discovered him living under a concealed identity, establishing himself as a successful businessman in the Bijbehara area,” it said.
"Long pursuit by the police team brought results, and the accused responsible for the death of innocent persons was arrested and produced before the TADA Court on 13th August 2026 for further legal proceedings," the police said.

At least 44 die as ferry sinks in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba
- Published
At least 44 people have died after a ferry sank on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe on Tuesday, police have said.
The ferry had a capacity to carry 90 passengers and five crew members but a lake official had reported that 120 people, including 12 children, were on it.
The vessel was hit by a strong wave and overturned, police added. Footage shared online appears to show the overturned hull floating in the water.
President Emmerson Mnangagwa has declared a state of disaster, as search and rescue operations intensify. So far, 77 people have been rescued.
Lake Kariba, which straddles the border with Zambia, is one of the world's largest man-made reservoirs, supporting transport and fishing and providing vital hydroelectric power to both countries.
An eyewitness, Maxton Kanhema, told AFP news agency that the boat had travelled in bad weather and may have been hit by a wave, causing its engines to switch off.
"People were in distress... there were bodies in the water and it was a sad situation to witness. Those that could be rescued were rescued," he was quoted as saying.
Mutsa Murombedzi, a local member of parliament, posted a video on X , externalof what she said was the boat at the start of the journey, adding that residents had been travelling across the lake to Kariba town, about five hours away.
"We have very hard questions that require honest answers. The officials must release the correct number of people who were onboard," she wrote.
The Zimbabwe Civil Protection Unit (CPU) said that registered ticket sales showed 114 adult passengers were on the vessel. An unknown number of children below ticketing age could also have been onboard, it added.
In its latest update on X, external, police said that 44 bodies had now been retrieved from the lake - up from the initial 15.
Local government minister Daniel Garwe said the president had declared a state of disaster to ensure "all necessary resources are mobilised" for search and rescue operations.
This included an army boat squadron, a police sub-aqua unit and a privately owned helicopter, he said.
"The government extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who have lost their lives in this tragic incident," Garwe added in a statement.

Can Sunderland defy the Premier League doubters again?
- Published
Sunderland were one of the stories of the 2025-26 Premier League season.
Promoted from the Championship through the play-offs in May 2025, the Black Cats marked their return to the top flight after an eight-year absence with a remarkable campaign.
Tipped for relegation by many, Sunderland ended the campaign in seventh to qualify for Europe for the first time since 1973.
So why - outside newly promoted teams Hull City, Coventry and Ipswich - are Sunderland once again among the bookmakers' favourites for the drop?
There are three main reasons their doubters can point to: their poor underlying numbers last season, the 'second-season syndrome' for promoted sides and a European campaign to contend with.
But are those reasons justified?
The underlying numbers
While results and where you finish in the table are ultimately all that matter, Sunderland's underlying statistics from last season suggest repeating their success might not be so simple.
Expected goals (xG) tells us how well teams do the basics of creating lots of good chances and limiting their opponents to few low-quality ones, based on how hundreds of teams before them have scored or conceded from those opportunities.
Only relegated Burnley and Wolves had a lower xG difference than Regis le Bris' side last season, while West Ham - with the fourth-worst overall xG - were also relegated.
While Aston Villa and Sunderland made a mockery of xG by finishing much higher in the table, the majority of sides finished mostly in line with their underlying numbers, showing those two overachievers were more the exception that proves the rule.
Indeed, the three sides with the best xG difference finished in the top three in the same order, while - excluding Sunderland - the five sides with the worst made up the bottom five.
Only Man City and Aston Villa overperformed their xG numbers by more than the Black Cats, who scored three more goals and conceded six fewer than expected given the number and quality of shots taken.
So taking the season as a whole, it seems that Sunderland's performances weren't as impressive as their results. But one event significantly affected part of the Black Cats' season: the Africa Cup of Nations.
They were without six players - twice as many as any other side - during the tournament in December and January. While the club's performances had already declined after a strong start, they suffered even more when their squad was stretched.
But once all those players returned, Sunderland's underlying numbers improved throughout the rest of the season and they ended the campaign playing like a mid-table side.
With no Afcon this season, the Black Cats may not suffer such a drop in performance. If they continue the 2026-27 season as they finished the last then relegation should be only a remote possibility.
Second-season syndrome
The belief that promoted sides that stayed up in their first season are often relegated in their second is a popular one, with the phrase 'second-season syndrome' regularly thrown about. But is it as common as people think?
Last season Sunderland and Leeds became the 53rd and 54th promoted sides to survive in the Premier League.
Of the previous 52, only 11 were relegated the following season (21%). The vast majority of promoted teams that stay up do not suffer from second-season syndrome.
However, there is precedent for a promoted side that had a first season as good as Sunderland's to be relegated in their second. In fact, the best promoted side in the 38-game era of the Premier League did just that.
George Burley's Ipswich ended the 2000-01 campaign fifth with 66 points - the highest finish and most points any promoted side has achieved in a 38-game season.
But with European football to contend with, they dropped 13 places and took 30 fewer points the next season as they were relegated in 18th place, with Sunderland the beneficiaries as they finished just one place above them.
Overall, four of the previous 20 promoted sides (20%) that finished in the top half in their first season suffered relegation in their second, with the most recent example being Sheffield United five years ago
The Black Cats were one of the sides that did not as they finished seventh under Peter Reid in 1999-2000 and followed up with another seventh-placed finish a year later (although that position did not bring European football back then).
The added workload of Europe
Sunderland will be playing in Europe this season for the first time in 53 years, with at least eight games in the Europa League on top of their usual domestic commitments.
They are the 10th promoted side in Premier League history to qualify for Europe and just the fifth to do so through their league position, with the others qualifying via cup competitions or fair play.
Despite their squads arguably being the least-prepared to handle the extra fixtures, five of the previous nine teams achieved another top-half finish and just two were relegated - Ipswich in the early 2000s and Hull in the mid-2010s.
Hull were an unusual case as they only finished 16th with 37 points in 2013-14 but qualified for Europe by reaching the FA Cup final.
Their European campaign lasted just four games as they were knocked out in the Europa League qualifying rounds in August and were relegated with 35 points the following May.
But then there is that Ipswich side again.
When Inter Milan knocked them out in the Uefa Cup third round on 6 December 2001, Burley's side had won just one of their first 15 games in the Premier League.
While they did find some form after that - they were 12th with 30 points after 25 games - just one win in their final 13 matches led to relegation.
Sunderland will be hoping to follow the example of the most recent promoted side to qualify for Europe - Wolves in 2019.
Despite playing 17 games as they reached the Europa League quarter-finals in 2019-20, they still had enough in the tank to finish seventh in the league again.
There are definitely the ingredients for Sunderland to have a difficult second season, but given how well-run they have been in their recent rise from League One to Europe, many fans will have faith they will continue to thrive.

No NALSAR 2026 student will be advocate: Bar Council after row over invite to CJI
The Bar Council of India has put the enrolment of NALSAR's 2026 law graduates as advocates on hold amid a row over students opposing CJI Surya Kant's invitation as chief guest at the university's convocation. The BCI has sought a report from the Vice-Chancellor and said enrolment could proceed if no indiscipline is found.
The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed that no student graduating from the National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR), Hyderabad, in 2026 be enrolled as an advocate by any State Bar Council until further orders, following a controversy over the invitation to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at the university’s convocation.
In an order, the BCI said, “Till further orders, no student of NALSAR University of Law, who has obtained the Law Degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any State Bar Council as an Advocate.”
The decision comes after a section of NALSAR students reportedly opposed CJI Surya Kant attending the convocation as chief guest. The development has raised concerns over the professional prospects of students graduating from the premier law institution this year, with their enrolment as advocates and, consequently, joining the legal profession potentially being affected.

20 December 2024 was a crucial moment for Luxembourg in supporting WHO and strengthening global public health, to make progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals in 2025–2028. A Strategic Partnership Framework (SPF) with the Ministry of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Affairs was signed amounting to €46.5 million – the largest-ever agreement WHO has had with Luxembourg. Furthermore, the first-ever multiyear agreement with the Ministry of Health and Social Safety €1 million was launched, as the country’s first voluntary contribution to WHO.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General greets with Luxembourg's Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety and Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. © MAE Luxembourg
“From now till 2028, this contribution will help finance priority areas in Luxembourg’s collaboration with WHO” said Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety during the bilateral meeting, “notably for sanitary crisis preparedness and response and the fight against health inequalities, with a special focus on gender.”
The amount of €46.5 million contains fully flexible and thematic funding, and allocations for the Universal Health Coverage Partnership, tropical disease research and polio eradication. The fully flexible funding enables WHO to allocate the money to the areas of highest need.
“By signing two new partnership agreements, we have reaffirmed Luxembourg's continued support for the WHO and its mission,” said Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. “This reflects our strong commitment to promoting global health and multilateralism. We launch these agreements with WHO because we believe the best way to avoid is to prevent.”
To support the achievement of WHO’s priorities, the strategic partnership framework with Luxembourg includes support for WHO’s core work to develop, deliver and implement high-quality technical products – the guidelines, norms and standards on which many countries rely.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, remarked how symbolic it was that the agreements were signed on the International Day of Solidarity. They are “a strong statement of solidarity by Luxembourg, not just with WHO, but with the people of the world”, said Dr Tedros.
Xavier Bettel, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Martine Deprez at the signing ceremony. © MAE Luxembourg
WHO and Luxembourg continue their historical strategic partnership, collaborating to fulfill a shared mission to promote, provide and protect health.

The youth movement in Bihar over the alleged examination paper leak took a violent turn in Siwan on July 25 during the Bihar Bandh called by the All India Students Association (AISA). The bandh was organised to protest the police lathi-charge on students during a massive youth demonstration in Patna on July 22 demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Violence erupted near J P Chowk in Siwan as protesters clashed with police. During the confrontation, police personnel opened fire using AK-47 assault rifles and pistols.
Three youths suffered serious gunshot injuries. They were identified as 15-year-old Mohammad Arif, 21-year-old Akash Yadav and 20-year-old Bullet Kumar Gond. All three were initially admitted to Siwan Sadar Hospital before being referred to Medanta Hospital in Patna due to the severity of their injuries. Shortly after the incident, videos showing blood-soaked Akash and Arif being rushed to hospital on a rickshaw circulated widely on social media.
According to the injured and their families, none of the three was participating in the violent protest. Arif, who worked at a local shop, was allegedly shot in the neck while returning home after closing the shop because of the bandh. Akash, a resident of Rae Bareli in Uttar Pradesh, had travelled to Siwan to celebrate his birthday with his fiancée and was allegedly shot while returning after buying a cake.
Bullet Kumar Gond said he was on his way to the district magistrate’s office to obtain caste and residence certificates when he was hit by a bullet in the leg. He further alleged that police assaulted him with fibreglass batons even after he had been shot and forced him to hop on one leg to the police station. “I was left writhing in pain for about an hour before an ambulance was called,” he said.
Following the incident, a video showing a police constable firing an AK-47 rifle went viral. Bihar Police suspended constable Abhishek Kumar after the footage surfaced. In a statement issued on July 27, Siwan Police claimed the constable fired four rounds into the air after being surrounded by protesters in order to protect lives and government property. The police further claimed that no one was injured in the firing. A departmental inquiry has been ordered, and Siwan superintendent of police Puran Kumar Jha said the investigation would also examine who authorised the firing.
However, an analysis by Alt News raises questions about the police’s official account.
Alt News examined videos recorded from multiple angles by bystanders and conducted geolocation verification of the footage. The investigation found that police fired at least nine rounds from AK-47 rifles at two separate locations. In addition, two separate instances of police personnel firing pistols were captured on camera. Geolocation analysis confirmed that these videos were also recorded in Siwan during the July 25 violence.
Eight Rounds Fired in front of Siwan District Commandant’s Office
Alt News obtained videos from three different vantage points showing a police constable firing an AK-47 rifle. The footage establishes that at least eight rounds were fired by him.
By matching the shops and buildings visible in all three videos, Alt News confirmed that the footage was recorded on the road in front of the district commandant’s office in Siwan.
One Round Fired on the Road to Kagzi Mohalla, Naya Bazaar in Siwan
At a second location, Alt News identified a police officer firing at least one round from an AK-47 rifle. The organisation obtained videos of the incident recorded from two different angles. By matching the shops and buildings visible in both videos, Alt News confirmed that the footage was recorded on Kagzi Mohalla–Naya Bazaar Road, around 400 metres from the district commandant’s office in Siwan.

Policemen Firing Pistol
Alt News also verified two separate incidents of police personnel firing pistols. In one video, matching nearby buildings established that the footage was recorded on the road in front of Darbar Jama Masjid in Siwan. A second video, showing a policeman firing a pistol towards protesters, was geolocated to J P Chowk by verifying the surrounding shops and buildings.

The findings contradict the police’s official version. While Siwan Police stated that only four rounds were fired from an AK-47, Alt News verified at least nine rounds fired from AK-47 rifles at two locations, in addition to two separate instances of pistol fire. The footage also shows more than one police officer firing towards protesters.
Speaking to Scroll, injured Akash Yadav said he was shot by a policeman wielding a pistol and claimed he could identify the officer who fired at him. He also alleged that the police may have pressured him to change his statement. So far, however, action has been taken only against one constable.
Police Firing in Jehanabad on July 23
The firing in Siwan was not an isolated incident. Two days earlier, on July 23, police also opened fire while dispersing protesters in Bihar’s Jehanabad district during demonstrations over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination.
Alt News found videos of the incident recorded from two different angles, showing police personnel firing sub-machine gun carbines towards protesters. Geolocation analysis established that the footage was recorded near the Child Development Project (Anganwadi) building outside the Officers’ Colony adjacent to Jehanabad railway station.
Geolocation:
Additional videos from Jehanabad showed police firing multiple rounds to disperse protesters gathered on the railway tracks.
Speaking to the media, Jehanabad district magistrate Tshering Y. Bhutia said police opened fire after protesters began pelting stones but claimed that no one was injured. He added that around 10 to 15 rounds were fired and that the situation was subsequently brought under control. Local residents, however, alleged that the number of rounds fired was significantly higher.
Political fallout
The Siwan firing quickly triggered a political storm.
Leader of Opposition in the Bihar assembly Tejashwi Yadav raised the issue on July 25, accusing the police of opening fire on students with AK-47 rifles. The following day, he visited the injured victims in hospital.
Samajwadi Party MP Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the use of AK-47 rifles against unarmed protesters, asking who had authorised the deployment of such a lethal weapon during the demonstrations in Siwan.
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi later spoke to injured Akash Yadav over the phone and assured him of assistance. During the conversation, Akash said he had been shot in the shoulder, leaving one of his hands impaired. He also told Gandhi that he had lost his mother in childhood, lived with his father and had no siblings. Referring to the Siwan incident, Rahul Gandhi alleged that the state’s response to student protests had become increasingly violent and criticised the use of AK-47 rifles against demonstrators.

Russian President Vladimir Putin’s visit to the disputed Kuril Islands has triggered a strong reaction from Japan, adding another strain to already tense relations between Tokyo and Moscow.
Putin visited Iturup, one of the southern Kuril Islands, on Thursday (August 13). Japan claims the island, which it calls Etorofu, as part of its Northern Territories. Tokyo described the visit as “absolutely unacceptable” and formally protested to Russia.
Putin’s trip was his first visit to the Kuril Islands as Russian president. He toured a fish-processing plant, a hospital and a school on Iturup, met local residents and held talks with Sakhalin Governor Valery Limarenko.
The visit came after Putin travelled to nearby Sakhalin Island, where he attended the final stage of exercises involving Russia’s Pacific Fleet and held a meeting on the security of Russia’s eastern borders.
The trip also carried broader political significance as Moscow continues to maintain a strong military presence in the region.
The dispute dates back to the final days of World War II, when the Soviet Union seized the islands from Japan in 1945.
Japan claims the four southernmost islands — Iturup, Kunashir, Shikotan and the Habomai islets — and refers to them collectively as the Northern Territories.
The territorial dispute has remained unresolved for decades and has prevented Russia and Japan from formally concluding a peace treaty ending their World War II hostilities.
Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi summoned Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev and lodged a “strong protest” over Putin’s visit.
Motegi said the Northern Territories, including Iturup, are Japan’s “inherent territory” both historically and under international law.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also condemned the visit, saying it was incompatible with Japan’s position on the Northern Territories and “absolutely unacceptable.”
She warned that the trip could make efforts to repair Japan-Russia relations even more difficult.
“We must say this visit has further hardened Japanese public sentiment toward Russia,” Takaichi said.
Moscow rejects Japan’s territorial claim.
The Russian Embassy in Japan called Tokyo’s protest “unfounded” and said the southern Kuril Islands were an integral part of the Russian Federation following World War II.
It also said Putin’s visit was a sovereign decision of the Russian leadership and was not something that could be discussed with foreign governments.
Putin has similarly argued that the current status of the islands reflects the outcome of World War II.
Despite defending Russia’s position, Putin said Moscow remained prepared to seek a solution aimed at concluding a peace treaty with Japan.
He also recalled the previously constructive relationship between Moscow and Tokyo, particularly under former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.
However, relations have deteriorated sharply since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.
Japan joined other G7 nations in imposing sanctions on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine and has provided financial and non-lethal defence assistance to Kyiv.
Putin has criticised Japan’s sanctions, describing them as “unprovoked” and accusing Tokyo of identifying Russia as a major threat.
The deterioration in bilateral ties has complicated efforts to resolve the Kuril Islands dispute and reach a peace treaty.
The Kuril Islands stretch from Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula toward Japan’s northern island of Hokkaido.
The archipelago has rich fishing grounds and mineral resources, while its location gives it major military and strategic importance.
Russia has strengthened its military presence on the islands, including deploying Bastion coastal defence missile systems and Su-35 fighter aircraft.
The military infrastructure gives Moscow greater control over regional sea lanes and reinforces its position in the territorial dispute.

Barely 200 kilometres from Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, where students and youth of the country came together in thousands to demand educational reform in India, a notice was served on a university, declaring that most of its built structures were illegal and would soon be demolished.
The institute, Mohammad Ali Jauhar University (MAJU), located in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, was established in 2006 by the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, founded by Azam Khan, one of the founding members of the Samajwadi Party. Khan, a former MP and 10-time MLA from Rampur, was one of the most powerful politicians in the region until the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in 2017.
MAJU is recognised by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and holds minority institution status. However, its staff and student body comprise people from varied backgrounds and religious communities, vice-chancellor (VC) Prof Zaheeruddin and students themselves told Alt News.
On July 15, the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) issued a notice to the university declaring that 38 of its 40 buildings were illegal and would be demolished within 20 days. The university was told to carry out the demolition itself, failing which, the RDA would carry out the demolition while charging the university expenses. However, the demolition order was stayed on July 28 by the chairman of RDA and the Moradabad divisional commissioner, Aunjaney Kumar Singh, till August 10.
Only a day after the notice, on July 16, a ‘counselling camp’ was set up outside the university’s main gate, the VC said. On the same day, the UP Public Works Department (PWD) declared an internal road belonging to the campus as a public road while installing signage, he alleged.
On July 27, Alt News visited the 475-acre campus on the first day of the semester. The buildings — designed, according to the VC, in the image of the White House and Turkish mosques — looked grand but lifeless as several structures stood half-built with construction abandoned mid-way. An air of uncertainty loomed over the campus and on the faces of the very few students who were present.
Some students, who were protesting the demolition, told Alt News that a student delegation had met the DM and sought written assurance that the buildings would not be demolished until the matter was decided by the Supreme Court. The DM gave only a verbal assurance and declined to put it in writing, they said.
‘All Buildings Constructed Before RDA’s Jurisdiction’
Zaheeruddin, who served as pro-VC and chairman of the department of law at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) before joining MAJU in April 2025, said that a prior show-cause notice had been issued on June 28 seeking a response from the university on the demolitions.
The university’s response was deemed unsatisfactory by the RDA, which called for a physical meeting on July 14, attended by registrar SN Salam and the institute’s legal counsel. The authority only heard their arguments for five minutes, and the next day, the demolition order arrived, said Zaheeruddin, adding: “This was completely unexpected for us. Our classes were running, admissions were fully underway. Compared to the past two years, more admissions were happening this year.”
The VC told Alt News the 38 buildings were constructed before 2016, when the university grounds fell under the gram panchayat, not the RDA. The RDA’s jurisdiction was extended to cover the land only through a notification in September 2024, he said, asserting that the authority is retrospectively taking action against buildings. “All buildings they have mentioned were constructed by 2016, when RDA had no presence in this area at all,” he said.
He further highlighted that multiple regulatory bodies — UGC, Bar Council of India, paramedical and nursing councils — have inspected and approved the university’s infrastructure over the years as part of their accreditation process.
Missing Paperwork & The 2019 Raid
The VC, however, did not want to show the approved maps to prove the buildings’ legality citing legal proceedings. “The matter is before both the divisional commissioner and the Allahabad high court. The university’s lawyers have advised against discussing legal specifics,” he said.
On the other hand, Salam, the registrar, offered a different explanation for the missing paperwork. He claimed that during a state-ordered raid in 2019, when police forces were deployed on campus, large quantities
of documents were seized. “They took so many documents, and we don’t know where they took them or find out which documents they took,” he said.
Salam recounted the 2019 raid, “As police and district officials raided the campus, the VC was confined to one floor, the registrar to another, the accounts staff locked elsewhere. There were media reports that around 8,000 books stolen from a 200-year-old madrassa had been recovered from the university. But when the matter reached court, only 26 books were produced.”
Both the VC and registrar claimed that during the raid, several books were destroyed, many of which were hand-written manuscripts. They also claimed that 42 large cupboards, purchased from Kolkata, with receipts and transport documents, were shown as stolen property. Alt News could not independently verify the claims made by the VC and the registrar on the 2019 raid.
The Sudden ‘Counselling Camp’
Exacerbating the adminstration’s and students’ worries after the notice was served, was the sudden counselling camp, allegedly set up the very next day to encourage students to enroll in other universities.
Among those at the camp were officials from Guru Jambheshwar University, Moradabad — a state university whose campus construction began in March 2024, currently operating from a temporary campus with just two rooms built, and teachers from Raza Degree College, Rampur. Their task, the VC said, was to inform prospective students that MAJU would soon be demolished and that they should apply for admission at Guru Jambheshwar University.
“I felt terrible, they were maligning us right in front of us, sitting outside our campus. I was shocked that government teachers were doing this and the district magistrate had set up the camp while we are still a functioning university,” Zaheeruddin lamented.
Arguing that the counselling camp amounted to contempt of court, he mentioned that the administration wrote to the Rampur DM citing a 2019 high court stay order that specifically ordered that students and staff of the university must not be harassed. The camp was removed after two days, on July 18 evening.
The Students’ Plight
When Alt News visited the campus, the students, now thrust into indefinite anxiety over their futures, were sitting in protest in front of the main gate, demanding that the RDA withdraws the demolition. “We are protesting since July 18 because RDA should withdraw this order. There are 3,000-4,000 students studying here, don’t snatch the pen from their hands,” said a 5th-year student from Panipat, Haryana.
Students echoed the administration’s account on the ‘pattern’ of state action which haunted their campus. Every year during admissions, they said, new action or rumours would surface, discouraging parents and prospective students. “Every year, fear is planted in children’s hearts that the university will be shut down,” said another student.
A student from Bareilly said his brother studied at MAJU between 2014 and 2017. After that, the perception in his area was that the university had already shut down. When he arrived for admission in 2015, he was urged not to enrol by several people in and around the area, with claims that the fees were too high and the university could collapse at any time.
The students further claimed that district officials attempted to curb their protest as the SDM arrived at the protest site on July 18 around 10 PM with policemen and asked the students to move their protest inside the campus, away from the main gate. District-level intelligence wing officials also called several parents, urging them to get their children to stop protesting, students alleged.
The students said they raised the issue with the district administration, which assured them that such pressure tactics would not be applied. Another protesting student mentioned that he had written twice to Saurav Das, the chief spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party, but had received no response at the time writing this report.
Alt News is withholding the names of the students who spoke to us in order to protect their identity.
RDA Officials Evade Queries
When we reached out to the RDA, we were re-routed through four different officials. We contacted RDA’s vice-chairman Ajay Kumar Dwivedi, also the district magistrate of Rampur, under whose name the July 15 notice was issued. His personal assistant, Ankush, directed us to the RDA secretary, Nitin Madan. The secretary, after answering some of our questions, directed us to the tehsildar, Ranveer Singh, who spoke briefly and redirected us to RDA assistant engineer Manoj Sisodia.
According to every official, only two of the 40 buildings had approved maps, obtained from the panchayat before RDA’s jurisdiction was extended to the area. The remaining 38, they said, had no approval from any authority — the Zila Panchayat, gram panchayat, or RDA. This formed the basis of the demolition notice, they said.
Upon being asked whether the matter could be resolved through compounding, a process where illegal construction is regularised by paying a fine and obtaining retrospective approval, Singh said it had been considered but rejected because the land use at the university site is not permissible under RDA’s current master plan. Sisodia, on the other hand, said that the university had never submitted a compounding proposal to RDA. However, the VC told Alt News that the institute believed that compounding was something RDA would initiate.
Further, we asked whether RDA had issued demolition notices to any other structures in the 62 villages that came under its jurisdiction since September 2024. Madan said “many have happened” without naming a single case. Ranveer Singh added “it keeps happening from time to time”, also offering no specifics. Sisodia eventually admitted that notices issued to other parties are “confidential and that the university’s case attracted attention only because it is a larger structure”.
“The university is in the wrong, but considering everything, the government, higher authorities, the courts, have taken their decision,” Sisodia said while acknowledging the dire condition of the students if the demolition is carried out.
The Azam Khan-Aunjaney Singh Connection
Parellel to all this runs another storied controversy between Azam Khan and Aunjaney Kumar Singh. During the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, complaints were filed by the then assistant development officer (panchayat), Anil Kumar Chauhan, and local BJP leader Akash Saxena against Khan for alleged hateful and provocative remarks against the then DM of Rampur, Aunjaney Kumar Singh, and other BJP leaders.
This led to Khan’s conviction in October 2022 with three years of imprisonment and his subsequent disqualification from the UP state assembly. His conviction was later overturned and he was acquitted by a higher court in Rampur.
Formerly an IAS officer of Sikkim cadre, Singh, hailing from Mau district in UP, notably has been serving as a government official in the state for 11 consecutive years now, and is presently on his sixth extension, which is set to end on August 14. Interestingly, in April last year, Singh accepted Khan’s plea against the imposition of Rs 20 crore fine in another case related to construction of MAJU.
According to Zaheeruddin, the demolition hearing, which was supposed to take place on August 3 at the court of divisional commissioner, has been postponed to August 10, bringing under scrutiny the apparent pendulum swing in the official relationship between Singh and Khan — from the district administration’s actions during Singh’s tenure as Rampur DM that culminated in Khan’s conviction, to subsequent administrative decisions that provided relief in matters concerning Khan’s university, and now the stay on the demolition proceedings.
The Unanswered Question
Beyond the missing approvals and the land use dispute, there is a deeper contradiction that neither the university nor the RDA addressed. During the April 2025 hearing concerning the Rs 20 crore labour cess fine, Khan had argued before the divisional commissioner that 10 of MAJU’s buildings were constructed by the UP PWD and UP Nirman Nigam using MP/MLA development funds.
Khan had then received relief after the divisional commissioner’s court nullified the cess fine imposed by the assistant labour commissioner (ALC) of Rampur. The same court, under the same authority of Singh, has now served a demolition notice to the institute. A pertinent question emerges: If state agencies built these structures with public funds, how did construction proceed without the approved maps?
Four government offices, multiple courts, contradictory bureaucratic positions and years of litigation have turned MAJU into a case study in administrative uncertainty. Whether the buildings ultimately stand or fall will be decided in court. Until then, it is not politicians or officials who bear the immediate cost of this prolonged impasse, but thousands of students who continue to attend classes while wondering if the campus they study in will still exist by the time they graduate.

Model Karlie Kloss and venture capitalist Josh Kushner may seem like an odd pairing on the surface, but they've been together since 2012 and have become partners in both life and business.
The couple has kept their relationship under the radar since they first started dating. Kloss and Kushner got married in October 2018 and held a second Western-themed wedding eight months later. They welcomed their third child in 2025.
Kushner also happens to be the younger brother of former White House advisor Jared Kushner, whose father-in-law is President Donald Trump. Josh and Jared Kushner's father, real estate developer Charles Kushner, became the US ambassador to France in Trump's second term.
Charles Kushner was also pardoned by Trump in 2020. He pleaded guilty to tax evasion, retaliating against a federal witness, and one count of lying to the FEC in 2005 and served two years in prison. As chairman of Kushner Companies, Charles Kushner admitted to filing false tax returns and recruiting a prostitute to seduce the husband of his sister, who cooperated with authorities, and film the encounter.
Although Kushner and Kloss haven't publicly spoken out against Trump, they have said they didn't vote for him in the 2016 election.
Here's a look at the relationship between Josh Kushner and Karlie Kloss, including their real-estate portfolio and ties to Donald Trump.
Josh Kushner, 41, founded the venture capital firm Thrive Capital in 2009, which helped make him a billionaire.
Thrive Capital has made some of its biggest investments in tech startups, including grocery delivery service Instacart, stock-trading app Robinhood, and insurance company Lemonade, according to PitchBook.
Because of his investments, Kushner sits on the boards for shaving product maker Harry's and wedding planning platform Zola.
The firm has also invested in companies like Instagram, Stripe, and ClassPass.
Kushner's savvy investments have made him a billionaire with an estimated net worth of $5.2 billion, Forbes reported in August. Thrive Capital was valued at $5.3 billion in January 2023 and reportedly manages about $25 billion in assets.
Kushner has also helped start two companies.
He cofounded health-insurance startup Oscar in 2012 and real-estate investment company Cadre in 2014.
Oscar, which aims to use tech to provide a more consumer-friendly insurance option, secured $375 million from Alphabet, Google's parent company, in 2018.
Meanwhile, Cadre was valued at $800 million in 2019, according to Forbes. Kushner founded it with his brother, Jared Kushner.
Meanwhile, 34-year-old Karlie Kloss began working as a model in her teenage years and went on to become a coding advocate.
Kloss skyrocketed to prominence as a Victoria's Secret Angel and became one of the highest-paid supermodels in the industry, Forbes reported.
She also runs a free coding camp for girls. In 2015, Kloss started Kode With Klossy, a charity that encourages girls to get involved in coding and tech.
Kloss and Kushner met and began dating in 2012.
On June 8, 2016, Kloss shared a photo on X, formerly known as Twitter, of her and Kushner revealing that she had met Kushner exactly four years before, placing their first encounter on June 8, 2012, although it's not known exactly how they met.
Their relationship became public when Kushner was spotted on Kloss' arm at a Victoria's Secret Fashion Show after-party in November 2012, Us Weekly reported.
They have tried to keep their relationship relatively private since then.
In 2013, Kloss said she appreciates that Kushner is "so not in fashion" in an interview with People.
"It's really refreshing to leave all the fashion shows and shoots and chaos totally behind," Kloss told People magazine.
Kloss deflected questions about her relationship in a 2016 interview with Elle.
Elle magazine's Lotte Jeffs asked Kloss if she and Kushner have a "no phones in the bedroom" rule. Kloss answered by shaking her head and saying, "I keep my phone pretty close to me." She added that she tries to digitally detox once a week.
When asked if technology ever causes arguments in their relationship, Kloss "deftly deflects the question," Jeffs wrote.
The couple has largely avoided talking about politics, which is notable given their ties to the Trump family.
Kushner is the younger brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law to former president Donald Trump and former senior White House advisor.
Josh Kushner told Forbes in April 2017 that he and Jared Kushner spoke every day, but refused to comment for an Esquire article about his brother in 2016 because he "did not want to say anything that might embarrass him."
However, the couple has publicly stated they didn't vote for Trump in 2016.
Kloss posted a photo of herself on Instagram in November 2016 filling out an absentee ballot. She included the hashtag #ImWithHer in support of Clinton.
Kushner's spokesperson told Esquire he's a lifelong Democrat and that he didn't vote for Trump.
"It is no secret that liberal values have guided my life and that I have supported political leaders that share similar values," Kushner told Forbes in 2017.
Neither Kushner nor Kloss attended Trump's inauguration in 2017. Instead, Kushner was spotted at the Women's March in Washington, DC, that weekend.
Kushner told other marchers he was there to observe, The Washingtonian reported.
Kloss also posted a photo on Instagram from the same Women's March, along with an Audre Lorde quote: "Women are powerful and dangerous."
In a 2018 interview with Vogue, Kloss distanced herself from the Trump family's political views.
"At the end of the day, I've had to make decisions based on my own moral compass — forget what the public says, forget social media," Kloss told Vogue. "I've chosen to be with the man I love despite the complications."
Kloss also pointed out the sexism in the questions she's frequently asked about her relationship with Kushner.
"It's frustrating, to be honest, that the spotlight is always shifted away from my career toward my relationship," she said. "I don't think the same happens in conversations with men."
Kloss and Kushner have also shown their support on social media for gun control.
The couple was spotted in March 2018 at the anti-gun-violence March for Our Lives protest in Washington, DC.
Kloss and Kushner didn't hide their presence at the march: They posted photos on Instagram from the March for Our Lives rally. A few weeks earlier, Kushner made a $50,000 donation to the anti-gun-violence group, Axios reported.
While Trump's first presidency was unpopular in Silicon Valley, Kushner's proximity to the White House didn't appear to slow his career as an investor.
"There is a lot of discussion in the Valley about political tests on both who you'll take money from and who you'll work with," the venture capitalist Marc Andreessen told Forbes in 2017. "Having said that, I haven't yet seen an instance of anyone hesitating to take money from Josh because of the affiliation with his brother."
In July 2018, Kloss and Kushner got engaged after six years of dating.
Kushner proposed "during a romantic weekend together in upstate New York," People magazine reported at the time.
"I love you more than I have words to express," Kloss captioned a photo on X announcing their engagement. "Josh, you're my best friend and my soulmate. I can't wait for forever together. Yes a million times over."
Kloss converted to Judaism shortly before getting engaged to Kushner, who is Jewish.
Kloss confirmed she had converted to Judaism in a March 2019 appearance on Andy Cohen's "Watch What Happened Live."
The couple got married in October 2018 in upstate New York.
The wedding was a small Jewish ceremony with fewer than 80 people in attendance, including Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump.
"So much love for you both as you begin forever together," Ivanka Trump wrote in a post on X.
Kloss wore a custom Dior wedding gown with lace sleeves and a flowing train.
"The wedding was intimate and moving," a friend at the ceremony told People magazine. "The couple was beaming with happiness."
In June 2019, the couple held a second wedding celebration at a ranch in Wyoming.
Kushner and Kloss' second wedding celebration was held at Brush Creek Ranch, an all-inclusive ranch resort near the Wyoming-Colorado border. The weekend included activities such as horseback riding, paintball, and off-road ATVing.
Photos shared from the wedding show that guests wore Western-themed outfits instead of traditional gowns and tuxedos. Attendees included Diane Von Furstenberg, Orlando Bloom, Katy Perry, Ellie Goulding, Princess Beatrice, and Ashton Kutcher.
Kloss and Kushner's relationship was publicly flamed on a 2020 episode of "Project Runway," which Kloss hosted for two seasons.
Brandon Maxwell, a judge on the fashion design reality competition show, criticized contestant Tyler Neasloney's creation. The assignment had been to design a look for Kloss to wear to a fashion event in Paris, but Maxwell told Neasloney that he couldn't see Kloss wearing the outfit "anywhere."
"Not even to dinner with the Kushners?" Neasloney replied, eliciting gasps from other contestants.
"Keep it to the challenge," Kloss responded. "You really missed the mark here, on all accounts."
When asked about the viral moment on "Watch What Happens Live" with Andy Cohen, Kloss said, "The real tragedy of this whole thing is that no one is talking about how terrible that dress was."
She added: "Andy, I'm sure I'm not the only person in this country who does not necessarily agree with their family on politics. I voted as a Democrat in 2016 and I plan to do the same in 2020."
The couple has three children.
Kloss and Kushner welcomed their first child, Levi, in March 2021.
Kloss revealed her second pregnancy on the red carpet of the 2023 Met Gala while wearing a black Loewe dress designed by Jonathan Anderson. Their son, Elijah, was born a few months later in July 2023.
Their daughter, Rae Florence, was born in September 2025.
Kloss occasionally shares photos of Kushner on Instagram, where she has 11.7 million followers, but she doesn't show her children's faces.
Kloss has posted photos of the couple traveling the world and celebrating Kushner's birthday, but she doesn't share much else about their relationship. She also keeps the faces of her young sons hidden in photos.
"I know in my life what really matters to me," Kloss said in an interview with Harper's Bazaar in 2018. "I'm not trying to hide that from the world. I just really like having a more private life."
During the 2024 election cycle, Kushner and Kloss each contributed to Democratic causes.
According to Federal Election Commission data, Kushner contributed $150,000 in February 2024 and an additional $100,000 in April 2024 to Growth Democrats, a political action committee.
Kloss also donated a total of $13,200 to Democratic congressional campaigns in 2024. She gave $3,300 each to Lucas Kunce and Debbie Mucarsel-Powell's Senate races and Whitney Fox and Rep. Darren Soto's House races, FEC data shows.
In 2024, Kushner and Kloss bought Life magazine and announced their plans to revive the iconic photography publication.
Kushner and Kloss bought the publication rights to Life magazine through Bedford Media, their media startup that also acquired i-D Magazine. They plan to revive the brand as both a print and digital publication.
"We see Life as an uplifting and unifying voice in a chaotic media landscape," Kloss, who serves as CEO of Bedford Media, said in a statement. "While Bedford is a new media company, we are deeply inspired by Life's iconic legacy and ability to connect diverse audiences with universal narratives of humanity."
They also purchased a $29.5 million beachfront house in Malibu.
The six-bedroom home is known as Wave House because its architect, Harry Gesner, designed the exterior to look like cresting waves. It was previously owned by Rod Stewart and Mo Ostin, a record executive who signed artists including Jimi Hendrix, Prince, and Madonna.
In June 2025, the couple attended Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos' lavish wedding in Venice.
Bezos and Sánchez Bezos tied the knot in a lavish wedding celebration held on the Venetian island of San Giorgio Maggiore.
Other notable names in attendance included Kim Kardashian, Bill Gates, and Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump.
Kloss and Kushner made their first Met Gala appearance in three years in May 2026.
Kloss wore a white Dior Haute Couture gown with an orchid headpiece to celebrate the 2026 Met Gala theme of "Costume Art."
They also attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding in July 2026.
Swift and Kloss' friendship dates back to 2013, but the pair hasn't been photographed together since 2018, sparking speculation of a falling-out. Kloss has maintained that Swift is a "close friend," telling The New York Times in 2018, "Don't believe everything you read."
Kloss and Kushner's attendance and Swift and Kelce's wedding appeared to confirm that the two are still in touch.
"Listen, I try to protect the privacy of my friends' personal lives," Kloss said when asked about the star-studded wedding on the "Today" show. "What I will say is that they're an amazing couple and I'm so happy for them."
Kloss said in an interview with Bloomberg in July 2026 that she has never met President Trump.
"I'm a Democrat," she told Bloomberg's "The Circuit" host Emily Chang. "I think it's possible to have relationships with people you politically don't align with. This country has always been a place for dialogue. We have to be able to talk to each other."
In August 2026, Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger agreed to purchase the Los Angeles Lakers in a deal valued at $12.5 billion.
Kushner and Iger are buying the Lakers from Mark Walter, a billionaire who also owns the Los Angeles Dodgers.
"As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world," Kushner and Iger said in a statement shared with Business Insider. "We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."
